newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - Wall Street Journal - Aug 7.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Wall Street Journal - Aug 7.

text.p: The following stories were reported in Thursday's electronic version of The Wall Street Journal.
* Microsoft said it will invest $150 million in Apple Computer.
* United Parcel Service and the Teamsters union will renew contract talks today.
* Hilton Hotels raised its takeover bid for ITT Corp to $8.3 billion, or $70 a share.
* Charles Schwab is in talks with three investment banks to offer its customers a part of the banks' IPO underwritings.
* Tobacco industry documents in Florida portray the industry's use of lawyers to foil regulators and mislead the public about the health risks of smoking.
* The economy moved into a higher gear in the early summer after slowing in the second quarter, according to a Fed survey.
* Bell Atlantic chief Raymond Smith said NYNEX CEO Ivan Seidenberg will have to prove himself before he leads the merged NYNEX-Bell Atlantic company.
* The new tax bill authorizes the IRS to accept credit cards in payment of tax bills.
* Federal Reserve chief Alan Greenspan asked the FASB to scrap plans requiring companies to adjust earnings to reflect changes in derivatives' market value.
* Bear Stearns was forced by changes in the tax deal to refund $40 million in fees to some clients.
* The Dow Jones Industrials rose 71.77 to a record, while bond prices rose and the dollar was mixed.
* The NASD is expected to stop mandating arbitration of discrimination and harassment cases on Wall Street.
* Continential Cablevision founder Amos Hostetter resigned.
* Thai officials asked the public to refrain from pulling funds from the country's banks and finance firms.
* Cabletron named NYNEX executive Donald Reed to head the company.
* A number of companies stand to win or lose should the three-day strike at United Parcel Service continue for more than a few weeks.
* Treasury Department today will auction $10 billion of 30-year bonds in a final installment of its latest auction.
